findings.forcedInvention: Who owns, and under what commit semantics, the binding of money movement to rights transfer. An implementer must invent whether escrow release and chain-of-title write are a single atomic commit or two independent operations, and which domain enforces it.
findings.claim: The cross-cut mechanism 'Atomic Payment <-> Rights Transfer' is ratified in domain-map-proposal.md and named by D-10 as one of the three thesis differentiators, but it has NO row in ideation-cx.md's consolidated 25-mechanism registry and is not among the 2 tracked candidates in that file's section 1b. Verified: the string 'Atomic Payment' occurs 0 times in ideation-cx.md, and 'atomicity' 0 times. Neither surviving mechanism covers it: the Split-Capture Trigger row explicitly scopes itself to capture and excludes disbursement ('Disbursement/collection is a phase-2 concern of domain 10 (Royalties) and is NOT part of this trigger'), while the Payments row pushes the rights leg away ('splits delegated to Split-Capture Trigger'). Each defers to the other and neither owns the binding. Worse, ideation-cx.md's own section 2 row 49 presupposes the mechanism exists ('The rights leg of the atomic commit lands in 09's chain of title') without any registry entry defining it. Section 1b states the promotion rule that makes this consequential: 'Downstream (`/create-prd`) MUST rule on promotion before any owning domain builds a private copy' — an unlisted mechanism gets no ruling and therefore gets built privately by whichever domain reaches it first.

Downstream (`/create-prd`) MUST rule on promotion before any owning domain builds a private copy`
findings.failure_scenario: Building the v1 session spine (D-31: domains 01, 02, 05, 07, 09-capture), an implementer reaches 05 Services Marketplace escrow release. Implementer A reads the Payments row's 'escrow releases only on satisfied condition' and ships escrow release as an independent transaction, with 09's chain-of-title record written asynchronously afterward — so a buyer who pays and receives delivery can end up with no committed rights transfer if the 09 write fails. Implementer B reads D-10's 'payment↔rights atomicity' and ships a single two-phase commit that refuses escrow release unless the 09 title write succeeds in the same transaction. These are different products: A permits paid-but-unassigned rights (exactly the failure the thesis exists to prevent), B blocks payouts on a rights-registry outage. Nothing in the four root files decides between them.

The ledger says sequencing is deferred to /plan-phase; the index says sequencing was resolved by D-31 and that /plan-phase no longer chooses a beachhead. It is the only `[OWNER]` tag in ideation-index.md, and it blocks a named taxonomy decision that D-75 itself says is unanswered. The item is labelled 'a VERIFY item' but no stage, person or file is named to verify it, unlike D-70's other loose end in the same decision, which IS routed ('flagged as `vision.md` Q-07').

findings.failure_scenario: v1 ships with the split-capture prompt delivered by web push. On iOS Safari the notification never fires unless the user has already added the PWA to the home screen — an install step nothing in v1 requires or prompts. The capture rate on the platform's single wedge metric (ideation-index.md:156 records the target as 'split-capture ≥60% @ 6mo') silently collapses for the entire iOS cohort. Nobody was assigned to verify the assumption before build, and the fallback behaviour when push is unavailable is specified nowhere: does the prompt degrade to email, to in-app only, or does capture simply not happen?

findings.claim: ideation-index.md's Progress Summary states that moscow-ledger.md lives one directory level up and is excluded from the file count. It does not: moscow-ledger.md is inside the ideation directory, `.memory/wiki/specs/moscow-ledger.md` does not exist, and the same index links it as `./moscow-ledger.md` 200 lines later. Two statements in one file about the same file's location, one of them false against disk. findings.failure_scenario: A downstream workflow or a `/audit-ambiguity` scope enumeration follows the Document Map's stated location, resolves `../moscow-ledger.md` from the ideation directory, gets a missing file, and either fails the scope check or silently proceeds without the ledger — the only artifact carrying MoSCoW tier for all 734 features. Conversely a build/copy step that trusts 'not counted ... live one level up' will exclude moscow-ledger.md from an ideation-directory copy on the belief it is not there, dropping the tier assignments that gate the entire release plan.

findings.claim: Two root files state different values for the cross-domain connectivity figure, and it is the exact figure both cite as the evidence resolving D-17 and justifying the keep-24-domains verdict. ideation-index.md D-26 says 211/276 (76%); ideation-cx.md says 206 live interactions and 206/276 (~75%), and the index's own Progress Summary says 206 (184 + 22). I parsed the section 2 table: it contains exactly 206 data rows (111 high, 66 medium, 11 medium·pending, 7 low, 11 low·pending — 184 non-pending + 22 pending = 206), so 211 is the outlier. Neither statement carries a marker or a reconciliation note.
